quest.title: Tales From the Court
quest.description: Livre seems to be fretting over something within the Palais Mermonia...

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: I repeat...

dialogues.speaker: Cornelia
dialogues.text: Mr. Livre. I understand your request, and I'm willing to assist you to the best of my ability, but... Well, please look at this application...

dialogues.speaker: Cornelia
dialogues.text: The person in charge here is Mr. Clapiers. All the materials you previously submitted are his to sort and deal with. Apart from him, none of us are permitted to handle them.

dialogues.speaker: Cornelia
dialogues.text: He's presently out on business. His official stamp is needed before your materials can enter our expenses calculation system.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Yeah, yeah! You know what? I've been here three times already — are you going to handle my case, or aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Cornelia
dialogues.text: Please calm down, Mr. Livre. There are only two people in Mr. Clapiers's office — the other is Mr. Monthois...

dialogues.speaker: Cornelia
dialogues.text: But he's getting on in years and is waiting to retire. In truth, he hasn't done any work in the office for a while now. He doesn't even draw a salary anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Then I'll just go to the office and make the old man stamp my stuff. Archons, I'll stamp them myself if I must!

dialogues.speaker: Cornelia
dialogues.text: I'm very sorry, but that won't do. First, it contravenes the rules, and second, the key to the stamp is with Mr. Clapiers, and only he can access it.

dialogues.speaker: Cornelia
dialogues.text: As for me, I have other things to attend to as well... Please believe me when I say that Mr. Clapiers will return and help you settle this matter today.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: ...Alright. Have a good day, Ms. Cornelia.

dialogues.speaker: Cornelia
dialogues.text: And you too, Mr. Livre.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Cornelia leaves in a hurry...

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Looks like I'll have to go home empty-handed, huh... *sigh*

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: Nothing, really. I just wasted my time — half a day, to be precise.

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: I've had it up to here with this Clapiers! The Palais Mermonia ordered a few clockwork meka from us, but they have yet to pay for them!

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: The first time I came to look for him, he told me that the office was doing an internal end-of-month audit, and could only dispense funds to external parties next month — as such, my application could not be processed.

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: The second time I came, he claimed that they were out of stamp pad ink, and their supplier's ink warehouse had caught fire, which meant that they needed to purchase some elsewhere. This in turn meant that my application could not be stamped.

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: The third time, he claimed that this External Assisting Personnel Registration Form had been updated and needed to be filled out again — and of course, they were out of forms, and new ones would only come in tomorrow.

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: I was going to come in today and get one, but now he isn't even in the office. Archons...

response.speaker: Rhemia
response.text: Hmm? Mr. Livre? Why do you look so upset? Can I help you with anything?

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: Officer Rhemia! It's so good to see you. This is what happened...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The story comes spilling out of Livre's rambling mouth...

response.speaker: Rhemia
response.text: Ah, Mr. Clapiers... He's not easy to get a hold of, for sure, but he really is on Erinnyes at the moment, and not in the Palais Mermonia.

response.speaker: Rhemia
response.text: Regardless, however, let's get the form for you first.

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: Eh? But Clapiers said that there weren't any more forms...

response.speaker: Rhemia
response.text: I have a way to help solve your problem. As I recall, some stores that have long-term arrangements with the Palais Mermonia have encountered the same issue you have.

response.speaker: Rhemia
response.text: Their solution is to regularly come to the Palais from time to time to collect forms and documents they might need.

response.speaker: Rhemia
response.text: This makes completing and submitting forms easier and quicker on the one hand, and keeps them abreast of changes made to said documents on the other... "It pays to be prepared," as they say.

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: Is... that how all the forms disappeared?

response.speaker: Rhemia
response.text: And that's why I'd say that these stores must have those extra forms, so let's pay them a visit.

response.speaker: Rhemia
response.text: Besides, I'm sure they'd be more than willing to help out once they've heard of your futile trips to the Palais.

response.speaker: Rhemia
response.text: Ah, yes. We'd best get the forms you need, fill them out, then bring them to Mr. Clapiers's office before office hours at the Palais end.

response.speaker: Rhemia
response.text: Would you be willing to help out, Traveler?

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: Traveler, please, help me! If I cannot get this done, I fear that another sleepless night awaits!

response.speaker: Rhemia
response.text: You just need to check out these two stores and try to borrow the newest version of the External Assisting Personnel Registration Form.

response.speaker: Rhemia
response.text: Let me see...

response.speaker: Rhemia
response.text: Please go to Estelle's smithy and Caron's clock shop.

response.speaker: Rhemia
response.text: Not long ago, the former helped the Palais repair street lamps, while the latter was involved in adjusting their clock.

response.speaker: Rhemia
response.text: They often take assignments from the Palais, so they're certain to have a form on them somewhere.

response.speaker: Rhemia
response.text: We'll be counting on your help regarding those locations, and in the meantime, Livre and I will split up and go to other shops.

choices.text: But what do I need to do?

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: What a pain... It's only a bit of Mora...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the External Assisting Personnel Registration Form...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You describe Livre's experiences and desire to borrow the form...

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: *sigh* Tough luck for Livre... I'm afraid I haven't any extras.

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: I brought a staff member from the store to assist me when I was repairing street lights at the Palais Mermonia.

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: Now, he was barely any help at all, so I didn't put his name down in the form.

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: But when it came time to hand the form in, Clapiers insisted that I put every last name down...

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: He even said that there would be "serious, unpredictable consequences" if I did not fill it out truthfully.

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: Seriously, it's just one missing name. What serious consequences could that lead to? Preposterous.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: So tiring... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the External Assisting Personnel Registration Form...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You describe Livre's experiences and desire to borrow the form...

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: This happens pretty often when you're dealing with the Palais Mermonia.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: I do have an extra form, so you can pass it to him.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: But I wouldn't let him get his hopes up about the Palais's work efficiency.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: Even if the form is submitted, it will take some time for the formal allocation of funds. And there's no use pressing them for it either...

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: No one has any surplus forms. What are we going to do...

dialogues.speaker: Rhemia
dialogues.text: Has the Palais Mermonia really been hiring contractors this often lately? Curious...

response.speaker: Livre
response.text: Oh my, oh my! You truly are my savior! If I had worked in vain one more time, I would surely have cast myself into a river!

response.speaker: Rhemia
response.text: May I ask you to... refrain from any behavior that might affect your personal safety and the city's image?

response.speaker: Rhemia
response.text: Whatever the case, please fill the form out first. Once you've done so, I'll get Ms. Cornelia to pass this on to Mr. Clapiers.

response.speaker: Rhemia
response.text: No matter how busy he is, Mr. Clapiers couldn't possibly ignore a form already on his table.

choices.text: I got your form right here.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: I don't know how I can thank you, Officer Rhemia. To be honest, I'd heard that you're still on vacation...

dialogues.speaker: Rhemia
dialogues.text: Helping the people of Fontaine is my duty as a police officer.

dialogues.speaker: Rhemia
dialogues.text: Alright, let's head out shortly. Any further delay, and we'll fall afoul of the Palais's punctuality with office hours.

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: Seriously, it's just one missing name. What serious consequences could that lead to? Preposterous.

dialogues.speaker: Caron
dialogues.text: When will the allocation be done, seriously...
